title: Particles Have Spaces Between Them
subject: Chemistry
objective: 50 mL of water plus 50 mL of alcohol gives only about 96 mL. The reason: particles of matter have spaces between them.

fill.q: Particles of matter have ____ between them.
Sugar dissolves because its particles go into the ____ between water particles.
Space between particles is least in ____ and most in gases.
Gases are easily ____ because their particles are far apart.

tf.q: 50 mL alcohol + 50 mL water gives exactly 100 mL.
tf.explain: It gives about 96 mL: particles fit into spaces.

tf.q: Gases can be compressed more than solids.
Particles in a solid have no space at all between them.
Dissolving sugar does not raise the water level much.

ar.r: Particles of a gas have large spaces between them.

ar.a: 50 mL water + 50 mL alcohol gives exactly 100 mL.
ar.r: Particles of liquids have spaces between them.
ar.explain: A is false (about 96 mL); R is true and explains why.

mcq.q: Space between particles is greatest in:
Mixing two liquids gives a smaller total volume because:

options: it fills the spaces between water particles

short.q: Describe an activity that shows particles have spaces.
short.solution: Mix 50 mL alcohol with 50 mL water: the total is about 96 mL, not 100 mL, because some particles fill spaces between others.

short.q: Arrange solid, liquid and gas by the space between particles, and give one consequence.
short.solution: Solid < liquid < gas. So gases compress easily and solids hardly at all.

match.explain: Spaces between particles explain mixing and compression.
